title: Designer: polishing an existing page
when: A page works but looks plain or messy, and the user wants it to look more professional without changing the content.
prompt:
Goal: A visibly better page through a few systematic changes to type, spacing and color, done as patches that keep the markup and content.
Steps:
1. Read the stylesheet and the markup; note the current fonts, colors and spacing values.
2. Fix type first: one body size around 1rem to 1.125rem, line-height 1.5 to 1.7, a clear heading scale, measure under 70ch.
3. Unify spacing: replace scattered values with a small scale and give sections consistent padding.
4. Reduce color: one accent for actions, neutral grays for text and borders, check contrast.
5. Add finish: focus-visible ring, hover on links and buttons, subtle borders or shadows on cards, a max width container.
6. Add the responsive rules that are missing so nothing overflows at 375 px.
Quality bar:
- Content and markup unchanged unless needed for a class hook.
- Every change follows the scale.
- Contrast and focus pass.
Pitfalls:
- Rewriting the whole stylesheet so old fixes are lost.
- Adding decoration (animations, gradients) instead of fixing basics.
- Changing the copy.
Verify:
- [ ] Type scale applied.
- [ ] Spacing unified.
- [ ] Focus styles present.
- [ ] No overflow at 375 px.
Output: Patched style.css with a short note of the changes.

examples.input: deixa essa pagina mais bonita, ta muito crua
examples.output: body 1.0625rem/1.6, sections padding 3rem, one teal accent, card borders, max-width 72rem
